rows.title: Nat.Finset, a bounded predicate-plus-bound pair, against Mathlib's nodup Multiset quotient Finset

axeyum.equality_regime_note: Literal Eq on the (membership-predicate, bound) pair, but this is NOT set-extensional equality: two Nat.Finset values differing only above their bound are literally distinct, per finset.rs's own doc (lines 26-28, 72-76: no quotient, no extensional set equality, every set-level statement is pointwise or via `beq`).

rows.reason: The carriers are not the same construction even loosely: ours is a computed bounded predicate whose own Eq is not set-extensional, theirs is a nodup quotient of lists whose Eq is set-extensional by construction, so no substitution identifies the two types.

witness.note: Landed 2026-09-05 (hall-singleton lane), after this repository's kernel-dependency-projection-v1.json was last regenerated -- present in source and in artifacts/facts/F-nat-finset-exists-memb-of-card-pos.json, absent from the projection id list, hence marked source-only rather than kernel-projection-verified. rows.title: Provable, a natural-deduction IPC derivation system with a soundness theorem, against Mathlib's algebraic Heyting order theory

axeyum.verification_detail: `Provable` and `ipc_excluded_middle_not_provable` confirmed present in the kernel projection; ipc_provable.rs:175 interns `Provable`, ipc_soundness.rs:1804 declares the theorem. The namespace is bare `Provable.*`, not `Ipc.*` -- a name search for `Ipc.` returns zero.
axeyum.equality_regime_note: Provable is a derivability relation (FormulaList -> Formula -> Prop) built by an eleven-rule inductive natural-deduction definition, not a carrier with an equality of its own.

mathlib.counterpart: HeytingAlgebra (order-theoretic; no proof-theoretic natural-deduction or soundness system exists in Mathlib for IPC)
mathlib.verification_detail: `class HeytingAlgebra (α : Type*) extends GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α, OrderBot α, Compl α where`, read directly at line 154. Mathlib.ModelTheory.* (Basic.lean, Skolem.lean, Ultraproducts.lean) is general first-order model theory, not IPC-specific. Mathlib.Tactic.ITauto is a decision procedure for intuitionistic tautologies, not a formalized soundness/completeness theorem. Case-insensitive search for 'intuitionistic' across the whole tree returns only the Heyting-algebra files and ITauto.lean -- confirmed clean negative for a natural-deduction IPC system with a proof-theoretic soundness theorem.
mathlib.equality_regime_note: An ordinary Eq-based algebraic typeclass, purely semantic/order-theoretic.

rows.reason: Ours is proof-theoretic -- a derivation system plus a soundness theorem connecting it to a semantics -- and Mathlib's is purely algebraic (an order-theoretic class) plus an unrelated decision tactic, so the two formalize different KINDS of object even though both are commonly called 'intuitionistic logic'.

witness.note: Refutes Provable FormulaList.nil (or (var 0) (imp (var 0) bot)) via the soundness theorem against a 3-element Heyting-chain semantics. Mathlib's HeytingAlgebra class states the algebraic laws a Heyting algebra must satisfy but proves no comparable non-provability-of-excluded-middle result for any natural-deduction system, because it has no such system to state it about.

rows.title: Nat.Rado's partition-regularity Rado numbers have no Mathlib counterpart at the pinned commit

axeyum.verification_detail: `Nat.Rado.IsRadoNumber`, `Nat.Rado.IsColouring`, `Nat.Rado.Arrows`, `Nat.Rado.schur_two` confirmed present; nat_prelude.rs:7410 interns the root, :8325/:8328/:8340 intern IsColouring/IsRadoNumber/schur_two.
axeyum.equality_regime_note: Literal Eq on Nat-valued colouring functions and bounds, same representation style as Nat.Finset/Nat.Graph.

mathlib.verification_detail: grep -rli rado Mathlib/ finds exactly one non-false-positive hit: Mathlib/Combinatorics/Compactness.lean, which formalizes Rado's SELECTION lemma (an infinite-combinatorics compactness/choice-function result, Finset.rado_selection) -- a different theorem by the same mathematician, not Rado's theorem on partition regularity of linear equations that IsRadoNumber formalizes (which generalizes Schur's theorem). Every other case-insensitive 'rado' hit across Mathlib is 'Radon' (measure theory), a false positive confirmed by reading filenames. Positive control: 'schur' (case-insensitive) also returns zero hits for Schur's theorem on monochromatic solutions in Mathlib/Combinatorics/, confirming the search methodology finds real hits elsewhere (Ceva, SimpleGraph, PMF all returned in the same session) and is not silently broken.
